summary: The paper proposes LayerBudget, a training-free online allocator that jointly picks a per-layer token-retention count n_l and a KV bit-width b_l in {4,8,16} by greedily maximizing a surrogate Q = coverage(n_l) x fidelity(b_l) x importance(l) per byte, plus a mean-fill imputation for evicted positions. The empirical sweep is unusually broad (7 models 7B-72B, MHA and GQA, 17 reimplemented baselines, 512-32K context, PPL/MMLU/GSM8K/NIAH/RULER/LongBench). My assessment as methodologist is that the empirical breadth does not rescue the core scientific claim. Three things break: (1) In the paper's own tables, plain INT4 quantization (KIVI) ties or beats LayerBudget on every metric that matters at 2-4x, dominates it at 6x, and Pareto-dominates it in the paper's own memory-vs-quality table (KIVI 9,990 KB @ 1.01 PPL vs LayerBudget 12,939 KB @ 1.07 at nominal 6x). (2) The paper's own ablation states that in the 1.5-3.5x regime -- where all the near-lossless headline numbers live -- no tokens are evicted and the Gini signal has no effect, i.e. the flagship joint-allocation contribution is inert exactly where the headline claims are made, and actively harmful where it does engage (joint 3.23 vs quant-only 1.00 at 6x on Mistral). (3) Memory accounting is mutually inconsistent across three places in the paper, the motivating 40 GB figure is off by ~15x under the paper's own equation, the fidelity constants quoted in the theory section disagree with the calibration appendix by 6x, and several baselines (SnapKV on MMLU) sit at or below chance, so the 'ranks 1st' ranking claim is not evidentially supported. Fatal-flaw gate (a) and (b) both trigger. I recommend rejection at this venue.
strengths: Empirical breadth is genuinely above the norm for this literature: 7 models spanning 7B-72B and both MHA and GQA, 17 reimplemented baselines behind a unified interface, four compression ratios, contexts from 512 to 32K, and six evaluation surfaces (WikiText-2 PPL, MMLU, GSM8K, NIAH, RULER, LongBench). Most KV-compression submissions report two models and one task.

Mean-fill is a cheap, cleanly isolated intervention with a large and replicated effect, and the controls are the right ones: logits KL 0.249 -> 0.009 on Mistral-7B and 0.6696 -> 0.0636 on Llama-2-7B at 6x, with median-fill and moment-matched random-fill reproducing the effect, which correctly isolates first-moment preservation as the mechanism rather than the specific statistic. This is the one component of the paper whose isolating experiment cleanly supports its claim.

The paper reports negative and self-undermining results that most submissions would bury: the leave-one-out bottleneck direction is measured on three architectures and found to contradict the authors' own inverted-importance default on Llama-2-13B (late +0.093 vs early +0.030) and to be flat on Qwen2.5-14B; the LayerBudget-KV variant's 4K NIAH collapse to 26.7% is disclosed in the limitations; and the MoE-nD and xKV head-to-heads carry explicit reimplementation caveats naming the specific confounds (harness, calibration, implementation gaps).

The profiling signal is well chosen from a systems standpoint: extracting only the last attention row per layer to compute the Gini coefficient is O(S) rather than O(S^2), which is what makes an online (rather than offline-calibrated) allocator plausible at all, and this is a real differentiator against KVTuner/ARKV-style offline sensitivity search.

The theoretical-properties subsection is honest in a way I want to reward: it explicitly declines the (1-1/e) submodular bound, states why (Q is a product and the action graph is not a matroid over the joint (n_l,b_l) action set), and correctly identifies the problem as MCKP with an impractical FPTAS. Papers in this area routinely assert submodularity they do not have.
weaknesses: FATAL (gate a) -- the method ties or loses to the fairest and strongest baseline on essentially every metric it reports. Main results table, PPL ratio at 4x, LayerBudget vs KIVI: 1.02/1.02 (Llama-2-7B, tie), 1.03/1.01 (Mistral, loss), 1.02/1.02 (Llama-3.1-8B, tie), 1.01/1.01 (Qwen3-8B, tie). At 6x: 1.17/1.02, 1.25/1.01, 1.08/1.02, 1.03/1.01 -- loss on all four. MMLU: KIVI equals or beats LayerBudget on 3 of 5 models (47.7/47.7, 60.1/60.1, 72.6/72.7, 76.1/76.6) and the one LayerBudget win is +0.4pp. NIAH at 4096: identical on Llama-3.1-8B, Mistral, Qwen3, Llama-2-13B, Qwen2.5-14B and Qwen2.5-72B; the sole difference anywhere is Llama-2-7B 100 vs 93.3, which at the stated cell size is one item out of fifteen. LongBench: 0.055/0.053, 0.040/0.041, 0.050/0.048 -- a tie. 72B RULER at 2x: 98 (LB) vs 99 (KIVI). Most damaging, the paper's own memory-vs-quality table at nominal 6x on Mistral-7B has LayerBudget at 12,939 KB with PPL ratio 1.07 against KIVI at 9,990 KB with 1.01 -- KIVI uses 23% less memory AND is better, i.e. LayerBudget is Pareto-dominated by a 2024 baseline in the authors' own table. The Byte-CR appendix argues the 2x allocator-side inflation is 'fixed across methods (H2O, CAKE, D2O, Ada-KV, KIVI, KVTuner all show similar median effective-CR ratios)', which if true preserves the ordering and therefore preserves the domination. Closing this requires a new experiment exhibiting a (model, CR, task) cell at matched effective bits/token where LayerBudget beats KIVI beyond a confidence interval -- not a reframing of the ranking to 'among token-compression methods'.

FATAL (P12) -- the contribution billed first has no measured marginal effect in the regime where the headline numbers are made, and a negative effect where it engages. The paper states it itself: 'At 1.5--3.5x: All signal variants are equivalent---INT4 quantization alone provides sufficient compression, no tokens are evicted, and Gini has no effect.' In that regime LayerBudget IS uniform quantization, which is why it tracks KIVI. Where the allocator does act, the component analysis (A1) gives quant-only 1.00/1.00 (Mistral 3x/6x) and 1.02/1.01 (Llama-2-7B) against joint 1.00/3.23 and 1.02/45.09 -- joint never beats quant-only at any cell in A1 and is catastrophically worse at 6x. The precision-level ablation (A3) is likewise degenerate: {4,16} and {4,8,16} give identical values in all four cells (1.02/3.23 and 1.02/45.09 differing only at 3x Mistral by 0.01), so the three-level bit set -- part of contribution 1 -- buys nothing measurable. Ranked by measured marginal effect the ordering is mean-fill >> inverted importance >> joint per-layer allocation ~ 0; the abstract's ordering is the reverse. The honest fix is to demote the allocator claim and reposition the paper around mean-fill plus importance direction.

FATAL (gate b) -- the importance prior is load-bearing, is not what it is named, and is known-wrong for one of the three architectures the authors probed. Eq. 4 defines w_l = sigma(k(1 - l/(L-1) - tau)) with hand-set k=5, tau=0.3: a fixed monotone function of normalized layer index. It is described as 'Importance weights each layer's contribution to eviction sensitivity', but it is never fit to, nor validated against, the leave-one-out sensitivity it claims to encode. The paper then measures the true direction and finds it inverted on Llama-2-13B (late-bottleneck) and flat on Qwen2.5-14B, and nevertheless reports all end-to-end numbers for those models under the known-wrong prior ('we... report end-to-end results under it across all models for consistency'), yielding Llama-2-13B 1.11 at 4x and 1.56 at 6x. A one-bit-per-model LOO probe is proposed as 'the recommended deployment recipe' but is never run end-to-end, so the paper has no results for the configuration it recommends. Per the gate, a limitation-section mention does not close this; the missing experiment is the per-architecture-direction run on Llama-2-13B and Qwen2.5-14B.

The surrogate objective is never validated against the metric the paper reports. Q(l,n_l,b_l) = C x F x w multiplies a dimensionless attention-mass fraction, a cosine similarity, and a sigmoid, then sums the product across layers under a byte constraint. No argument is given that sum_l Q is monotone in (or even correlated with) the WikiText-2 PPL ratio actually reported, and no such correlation is ever measured. Only the coverage factor is validated, on one model (Mistral, MAE 3.1%), and coverage validation is against attention mass captured -- not against quality. The additive form is also unmotivated: quality composes multiplicatively through the residual stream, and an additive per-layer surrogate assumes independence that the paper's own LOO analysis (restoring layers 0-1 alone recovers 1.8-2.0 PPL) contradicts. The greedy's reported '118--119%' figure has no stated reference object, so it certifies nothing -- it is not an approximation ratio against the MCKP optimum, which the paper correctly says it cannot bound.

Memory accounting is mutually inconsistent in three places, and the reconciliation appendix contradicts a results table. (i) The Byte-CR appendix asserts 'every method's effective CR (= Full_KV_bytes / method_bytes) matches its nominal CR within +/-0.05 at the points reported'. (ii) The KV-memory-savings table at nominal CR=2x reports savings of 24.3% (Llama-2-7B), 42.9% (Mistral-7B) and 71.2% (Llama-3.1-8B), i.e. effective CRs of 1.32x, 1.75x and 3.47x -- three different values, none of them 2x, all far outside +/-0.05. (iii) The memory-vs-quality table at nominal 6x gives 12,939/39,296 = 3.04x. Four denominators are in play across the paper (nominal, token-count, allocator-side, mean_memory_bytes) and the paper resolves them by promising a camera-ready regeneration. Since CR is the x-axis of every claim in the paper, this must be fixed before, not after, review.

Arithmetic error in the same memory table: Llama-3.1-8B and Mistral-7B have identical KV geometry (32 layers, 8 KV heads, head_dim 128), so their base KV at S=512 must be identical, yet the table reports 189 MB and 95 MB -- a factor of exactly 1.99, so one row double-counts K and V. By the paper's own Eq. in the introduction, 2 x 32 x 512 x 8 x 128 x 2 bytes = 67 MB for both. The 'GQA models achieve 43--72% memory savings' claim, repeated three times in the paper, is computed from these two mutually inconsistent rows.

The motivating number in the first paragraph is wrong by roughly an order of magnitude under the paper's own formula. 'At FP16, Llama-2-70B at 8K context requires over 40 GB': with L=80, 8 KV heads (Llama-2-70B is GQA), d=128, S=8192, b=2, the paper's own expression 2 L S H d b gives 2 x 80 x 8192 x 8 x 128 x 2 = 2.68 GB. Even assuming no GQA (64 heads) gives 21.5 GB. Neither reaches 40 GB at batch 1.

The fidelity constants used in the theory section disagree with the calibration appendix by 6x. Section 3.5 argues diminishing returns from 'Delta F_{4->8} = 0.0035 > Delta F_{8->16} = 0.0001', but the per-model calibration table gives mean F(8) = 0.9998 and mean F(4) = 0.977, hence Delta F_{4->8} = 0.022 and Delta F_{8->16} = 0.0002. Since these constants set the ratio Delta Q / Delta M for the upgrade_bits action, they determine the entire greedy trajectory; the allocator must be rerun with the calibrated values and all results restated.

The allocator-latency extrapolation contradicts its own measurement by 8x. '<1 ms in isolation on Mistral-7B at S=1024' over L x S/Delta n = 32 x 1024/8 = 4096 iterations implies at best ~244 ns per iteration. The Qwen2.5-72B/32K projection then assumes '~30 ns per iteration (a single floating-point comparison)' to reach '~10 ms'. At the paper's own measured rate, 327,680 iterations cost ~80 ms per allocation, which is not 'small relative to a single decode step' (measured TPOT is 20-93 ms). Either measure the 72B/32K allocation directly or drop the projection.

Several baselines are at or below chance, which invalidates the ranking claim. On MMLU (4-way, chance = 25%), SnapKV scores 27.1 / 29.6 / 29.4 / 33.4 / 41.2 against Full KV 47.3 / 63.9 / 60.2 / 72.9 / 76.6, and H2O 36.5-54.4. Published SnapKV and H2O are near-lossless on MMLU at these budgets. The paper audits only H2O, and the audit itself returns 29.4% for a 'faithful per-head H2O matching the official FMInference/H2O algorithm' -- also chance -- which is evidence the harness is broken, not evidence the collapse is real. Corroborating: the LongBench table has Full KV at 0.056 / 0.040 / 0.050 where LongBench F1/ROUGE-L is normally in the 20-45 range, and H2O at 0.097 on Llama-2-7B, nearly 2x Full KV, footnoted away as degenerate repetition. Under a harness where Full KV scores 0.05, 'LayerBudget matches Full KV on all models' carries no information. The headline 'ranks 1st among all token-compression methods' and 'H2O at 4x collapses (83x PPL)' both rest on this harness.

'Ours' denotes different configurations in different tables, and the mean-fill headline is computed against the wrong one. The importance-direction ablation gives Inverted (the stated default) at 6x zero-fill as 1.283 (Mistral) and 2.52 (Llama-2-7B). Three other tables -- the zero-fill deployment table, the budget sweep, and the component analysis -- report LayerBudget at the same model/CR/fill as 3.23 and 45.09, which are exactly the Sigmoid (late-high) rows of the ablation. The Analysis claim 'On Llama-2-7B, PPL ratio also improves from 45.09 to 1.13 at 6x (97.5% reduction)' is therefore measured from the non-default sigmoid configuration, not from the method as defined in the abstract. Every table must be restated under one declared configuration.

The abstract contradicts the tables in three places. (i) 'PPL ratio <= 1.03 at 4x on seven models from 7B to 72B' -- Llama-2-13B is 1.11 at 4x and 1.56 at 6x in the large-model scaling table; the parenthetical 'at GQA' silently excludes the counterexample. (ii) 'at CR=4x and 4096 tokens, LayerBudget matches Full KV accuracy on every model (100...' -- the NIAH table gives Mistral-7B 73.3 at 4x against Full KV 86.7. (iii) 'ranks first among token-compression methods at 2--4x at memory-matched comparison' -- the memory-matched appendix is referenced but never shown, and the one memory table that is shown has LayerBudget using more bytes than KIVI at worse quality.

Positioning and evaluation are a generation behind the field. The claim 'To our knowledge, no prior online, training-free method jointly optimizes per-layer (n_l, b_l)' is not defensible against the 2026 literature: RDKV casts eviction and quantization as endpoints of one bit-allocation problem via reverse water-filling and is training-free and post-prefill; HqeKV (ACL 2026 Findings, code public) is a hybrid quantization+eviction optimizer with a joint K-V importance metric; ThinKV and ARKV occupy the same space. None is cited or compared. The evaluated envelope is 2-6x while the current bar is 14-40x (MoE-nD 14x, STAR-KV 20x, KVTC 20-40x, ThinKV <5% cache retention). Benchmarks the community now expects are absent: LongBench-v2 (v1 is dated and here evidently broken), InfiniteBench, SCBench, HELMET, effective bits/token as a common currency, and RULER beyond a single 4K point on one model. The 2026 methodology results are also unaddressed -- query-aware vs query-agnostic compression ordering, and the finding that swapping sdpa->eager shifts RULER by -0.221, larger than most method gaps (the paper discloses SDPA only for the long-context runs and never states the short-context backend).

The mechanistic evidence is from a model that is never evaluated. Both mechanism figures (allocation_heatmap, signal_curves), the '2.1x Gini spread' claim in the introduction, and the complementarity statistic rho = 0.194 are all on TinyLlama-1.1B, which appears in no results table. Over a 22-layer model, rho = 0.194 is not significantly different from zero (p ~ 0.39), so 'Weak correlation (rho=0.194) confirms complementary signals' is unsupported -- and 'weak correlation implies complementary information' is in any case a non-sequitur; two uninformative signals are also weakly correlated.

The systems result is negative and under-reported for a paper whose premise is a memory bottleneck. The memory table's own footnote reads 'Speedup <1x due to compression overhead'; decode TPOT overhead is +2.6% to +12.2%; the full profiling pipeline adds 61-109% to prefill; there is no custom kernel; and the vLLM/PagedAttention path is validated only at 512 tokens. Meanwhile the majority of results are at S=512-1024, where the KV cache is 67-287 MB and is not a bottleneck on any of the stated GPUs -- the claims are stated over the long-context regime but the evidence is dominated by the short-context regime.

Presentation/format (noted for completeness, weighted lightly given my brief): the source as supplied would not compile -- '\begin{table[t]' is malformed, '\section{Analysis' and '\textbf{Downstream accuracy.' have unclosed braces, and the LongBench sentence terminates mid-clause ('On LongBench (16 English tasks, Table~[REF]') with the Limitations block swallowed into the Analysis section. This is a desk-reject-adjacent format risk under the NeurIPS style requirement.
questions: Under a single declared denominator (pipeline-measured mean_memory_bytes) with effective bits/token reported alongside, is there ANY (model, CR, task) cell in which LayerBudget beats KIVI by more than the paired-bootstrap 95% interval? If yes, please show that cell with its interval. If not, the 'ranks 1st' claim should be explicitly restricted to token-eviction methods in the abstract, and the paper's contribution restated accordingly.

KIVI's PPL rows are literally constant across 2x/3x/4x/6x (1.006 four times on Mistral, 1.02 four times on Llama-2-7B), while the setup section says pure quantization 'caps at ~4x at INT4'. What does the CR knob actually change for KIVI, and what are KIVI's measured mean_memory_bytes at each nominal CR on Mistral-7B at 512 tokens? Without this the KIVI comparison is not memory-matched in either direction.

Which importance configuration produced the LayerBudget rows in the zero-fill deployment table, the budget sweep, and the component analysis? The values 3.23 (Mistral 6x) and 45.09 (Llama-2-7B 6x) match the Sigmoid row of the importance ablation, not its Inverted row (1.283 and 2.52), yet inverted is the stated default. If the mean-fill 45.09 -> 1.13 improvement was measured against the sigmoid configuration, what is the corresponding improvement from the inverted default (2.52 -> ?)?

Do the eviction baselines (H2O, SnapKV, CAKE, D2O, Ada-KV) receive mean-fill in the main results table and in the 16K/32K long-context table, or is mean-fill applied only to LayerBudget? The introduction implies H2O is evaluated with mean-fill somewhere ('even with mean-fill... H2O at 2x degrades 6--16%') but the table captions state mean-fill as a property of the LayerBudget configuration.

Do you measure any correlation between the surrogate sum_l Q(l, n_l, b_l) and the PPL ratio you report? A scatter of surrogate objective against measured PPL ratio over the allocator's search trajectory would establish that the greedy is optimizing the right thing; without it, the '118--119%' figure (of what reference?) does not certify solution quality.

Please reconcile the base-KV entries of 189 MB (Llama-3.1-8B) and 95 MB (Mistral-7B) at S=512 in the memory-savings table, given that both models have 32 layers, 8 KV heads and head_dim 128 and must therefore have identical FP16 KV footprints (67 MB by your own equation). Which of the two rows is correct, and how does the correction change the '43--72% memory savings' claim?

SnapKV scores at or below 4-way chance on MMLU for all five models in your table. What budget, observation window and pooling did you use, and can your harness reproduce the published SnapKV and H2O MMLU numbers on any single (model, budget) point before being used to rank 17 methods?

The recommended deployment recipe is a per-architecture importance direction set from a 5-prompt LOO probe, but no end-to-end results are reported under it. What are the Llama-2-13B and Qwen2.5-14B PPL/NIAH numbers at 4x and 6x with the per-architecture direction, and how do they compare to KIVI at matched bytes?

probe_answers.answer: Alternatives that plausibly solve the same problem: (1) KIVI (uniform INT4 KV quantization) -- compared head-to-head, and it wins or ties: main results 4x LB/KIVI = 1.02/1.02, 1.03/1.01, 1.02/1.02, 1.01/1.01; 6x = 1.17/1.02, 1.25/1.01, 1.08/1.02, 1.03/1.01; MMLU KIVI >= LB on 3 of 5; NIAH identical on 6 of 7 models; memory-vs-quality table KIVI 9,990 KB @1.01 vs LB 12,939 KB @1.07. The paper handles this not by beating it but by redefining the ranking population ('ranks 1st among token-compression methods'), which excludes the winner. (2) RDKV (rate-distortion joint eviction+quantization by reverse water-filling, training-free, post-prefill, 97.81% of full-cache accuracy at 2.48% retention, 4.5x decode speedup at 128K) -- IGNORED entirely, and it directly falsifies the paper's novelty sentence 'no prior online, training-free method jointly optimizes per-layer (n_l, b_l)'. (3) HqeKV (ACL 2026 Findings, hybrid quantization+eviction with an integrated per-element action selector and a joint K-V importance metric, public code) -- IGNORED. (4) ThinKV (hybrid quantization+eviction, ~3.4 average bits, near-lossless at <5% cache) and ARKV (per-layer original/quant ratios from prefill attention statistics) -- IGNORED. (5) NVIDIA KVPress, the de-facto harness with 30+ methods, a public leaderboard, and built-in PerLayerCompressionPress and QuantizedCache -- IGNORED; the paper hand-reimplements 17 baselines instead, and the resulting SnapKV/H2O MMLU numbers sit at chance. (6) Trivial 'keep start + recent window' -- present as StreamingLLM, correctly. Two defects: an obvious alternative (KIVI) is compared and wins on the metric that matters; four directly overlapping 2026 systems are ignored while a strong novelty claim is made against them.

(1) Q(l, n_l, b_l), the 'quality model' (Eq. 3) -- never given units or a referent; it is the product of a mass fraction, a cosine similarity and a sigmoid, summed across layers, and its relation to the reported PPL ratio is never stated or measured. (2) S -- overloaded: total sequence length in the memory formula, the coverage denominator in Eq. 4, and implicitly the growing decode-time length; the paper never says whether allocation is recomputed as S grows. (3) CR -- overloaded four ways: nominal, token-count, allocator-side, and pipeline mean_memory_bytes, with three mutually inconsistent values for the same nominal point (see P5). (4) w_l -- named 'importance... eviction sensitivity' but computed as a fixed positional sigmoid, never fit to any sensitivity measurement; the same word 'importance' also denotes the measured LOO improvement in Section 5, which has the opposite sign on Llama-2-13B. (5) B, the memory budget -- appears in the constraint and in Algorithm 1 but is never mapped to a target CR; the reader cannot tell how a '4x' run sets B. (6) n_min = sink + recent -- neither sink count nor recent-window size is ever given numerically, anywhere. (7) Delta n = 8 in the allocator vs 16-token block rounding in the vLLM path -- two granularities, never reconciled. (8) 'Fill' mode -- mean-fill in the main tables, zero-fill in the ablations, never controlled across tables, and results are cross-referenced between them. (9) 'FP16 KV reference' for the PPL ratio -- all models run 4-bit weights, so the reference is itself a quantized model; never stated whether the denominator is FP16-weights or 4-bit-weights full-KV. (10) 'LB' vs 'LayerBudget' vs 'LayerBudget-KV' -- the NIAH and memory tables use 'LB' without defining it. (11) '118--119%' -- percentage of what reference is never stated. Eleven found; the count itself is a defect.

Four recomputations, three fail. (a) MOTIVATING NUMBER. 'At FP16, Llama-2-70B at 8K context requires over 40 GB.' Using the paper's own expression 2 L S H d b with Llama-2-70B (L=80, 8 KV heads GQA, d=128, S=8192, b=2 bytes): 2 x 80 = 160; 160 x 8192 = 1,310,720; x8 = 10,485,760; x128 = 1,342,177,280; x2 = 2,684,354,560 bytes = 2.68 GB. Even assuming MHA (64 heads) gives 21.5 GB. FAILS by ~15x (or ~2x under the most charitable reading). (b) BASE KV IN THE MEMORY TABLE. Mistral-7B and Llama-3.1-8B both have 32 layers, 8 KV heads, d=128. At S=512: 2 x 32 x 512 x 8 x 128 x 2 = 67,108,864 bytes = 67 MB for BOTH. The table reports 95 MB and 189 MB -- a ratio of 1.99 between two architecturally identical caches. FAILS; one row double-counts K and V. Downstream, the savings column gives 24.3%/42.9%/71.2% at nominal CR=2x, i.e. effective 1.32x/1.75x/3.47x -- none equal 2x. (c) FIDELITY DELTAS. Section 3.5 states Delta F_{4->8} = 0.0035 > Delta F_{8->16} = 0.0001. From the calibration table, mean F(8) = (0.9998+0.9997+0.9999+0.9997+0.9998+0.9999)/6 = 0.99980 and mean F(4) = (0.9794+0.9758+0.9817+0.9683+0.9781+0.9810)/6 = 0.97738. Delta F_{4->8} = 0.9998 - 0.9774 = 0.0224 (6.4x larger than stated); Delta F_{8->16} = 1.0000 - 0.9998 = 0.0002. FAILS; and because these constants set Delta Q for the upgrade_bits action, the greedy trajectory itself is affected. (d) ALLOCATOR LATENCY. '<1 ms in isolation on Mistral-7B at S=1024' over L x S/Delta n = 32 x 1024/8 = 4096 iterations implies >= 244 ns/iteration. The 72B/32K projection uses 80 x 32768/8 = 327,680 iterations (this count CHECKS OUT) but assumes ~30 ns/iteration to obtain ~10 ms. At the paper's own measured 244 ns/iteration the same 327,680 iterations cost ~80 ms -- 8x the projection, and comparable to the measured 82-93 ms TPOT on Qwen2.5-14B. FAILS. (e) Mean-fill reductions DO check out: 1 - 0.009/0.249 = 96.4%; 1 - 0.0636/0.6696 = 90.5%.

The two most quotable numbers in the abstract both rest on baselines whose configuration the paper's own data shows to be broken. (1) 'At 32K context on Mistral-7B, H2O at 4x collapses (83x PPL)': in the MMLU table the same H2O implementation scores 36.5/42.2/46.8/52.0/54.4 against Full KV 47.3/63.9/60.2/72.9/76.6, and SnapKV scores 27.1/29.6/29.4/33.4/41.2 -- at or below 4-way chance (25%). Published SnapKV and H2O are near-lossless on MMLU at these budgets. The paper attempts an audit and the audit returns 29.4% for a 'faithful per-head H2O matching the official FMInference/H2O algorithm', i.e. it reproduces chance and concludes the collapse is real; the correct inference is that the harness, not the method, is at fault. (2) 'ranks first among token-compression methods': a ranking over a population containing chance-level baselines is uninformative. Corroborating harness evidence: the LongBench table has Full KV at 0.056/0.040/0.050 where LongBench F1/ROUGE-L is normally 20-45, and H2O at 0.097 on Llama-2-7B (nearly 2x Full KV) explained away as degenerate repetition. Is the most favorable-sounding abstract number the honest one? No. The honest headline from these tables is 'LayerBudget matches uniform INT4 quantization at 2-4x and is worse at 6x'.

Seven internal contradictions. (1) The Byte-CR appendix states 'every method's effective CR ... matches its nominal CR within +/-0.05', while the memory-savings table at nominal CR=2x gives effective 1.32x / 1.75x / 3.47x on three models, and the memory-vs-quality table at nominal 6x gives 12,939/39,296 = 3.04x. (2) 'pure quantization (KIVI) caps at ~4x at INT4' vs KIVI rows reported at 6x with 1.01-1.02; KIVI's values are literally identical across 2/3/4/6x (1.006 four times), so its nominal CR label is doing nothing. (3) Abstract 'PPL ratio <= 1.03 at 4x on seven models from 7B to 72B' vs Llama-2-13B = 1.11 at 4x, 1.56 at 6x. (4) Abstract/Analysis 'LayerBudget matches Full KV accuracy on every model (100...' on NIAH at 4x vs the NIAH table's Mistral-7B 73.3 against Full KV 86.7. (5) Section 3.5 Delta F_{4->8} = 0.0035 vs the calibration table's 0.0224. (6) 'Ours' means different things in different tables: the importance ablation gives Inverted (the declared default) at 6x zero-fill as 1.283 (Mistral) / 2.52 (Llama-2-7B), while the zero-fill deployment table, the budget sweep and the component analysis all report LayerBudget at those same cells as 3.23 / 45.09 -- the Sigmoid row's values. The mean-fill headline '45.09 -> 1.13 (97.5%)' is therefore computed off the non-default configuration. (7) Section 3.5 claims 'The quantize first behavior emerges naturally from the marginal gains', while the ablation states that at 1.5-3.5x 'no tokens are evicted and Gini has no effect' -- i.e. the behavior is a consequence of the budget being loose, not of the marginal-gain ordering discriminating anything. Related: the Related Work paragraph sells LayerBudget-KV as beating both LayerBudget and MoE-nD at 6x without mentioning that limitation (5), pages later, discloses its 4K NIAH drops to 26.7%.

The prose shows machine-assisted or rebuttal-derived construction in specific places, though most of the paper reads as ordinary technical writing. (a) Rebuttal artifacts embedded in a submission: the Related Work MoE-nD paragraph is a single ~400-word block that argues a defense rather than positioning ('The two design points are therefore best read as complementary operating regimes of the same framework rather than two competing solvers'; 'any divergence from the original authors reported numbers should be attributed to (a)... (b)... (c)... we will update against their official code at camera-ready'). An entire appendix ('Byte-CR Reconciliation') exists solely to answer an accounting objection and closes with 'For the camera-ready we will regenerate Table X' -- a promissory erratum, not a result, and it presumes acceptance. (b) 'Not X but Y' reframings used to convert losses into design points: 'we therefore treat inverted importance as a Mistral-tuned default, not a universal principle'; 'the 2x inflation in the table below is allocator overhead, not a CR-denominator inconsistency between methods'; 'the value is the measured ratio (not a typo)'. (c) Description-not-argument: the Key findings bullet list restates table cells in uniform rhythm ('LayerBudget achieves near-lossless compression at 2-4x', 'LayerBudget is the best method that reduces token count', 'LayerBudget ranks 1st among all token-compression methods' -- bullets 1, 2 and 4 make the same claim three times) without ever confronting the KIVI column sitting in the same table. (d) Structural evidence of automated assembly: '\begin{table[t]', unclosed '\section{Analysis' and '\textbf{Downstream accuracy.', and a sentence that stops mid-clause ('On LongBench (16 English tasks, Table~[REF]') immediately before the Limitations text -- the Analysis section has effectively been swallowed. I flag this as a credibility defect, not a typography note.

(a) OVER-ASSERTION. 'Nearly all existing methods apply their strategy uniformly across layers' -- contradicted two pages later by the paper's own list of PyramidKV, D2O, SqueezeAttention, CAKE, Ada-KV and KVTuner, all of which vary allocation by layer or head. 'The optimal strategy is therefore to exhaust quantization headroom before evicting tokens' -- 'optimal' is asserted with no argument, and the paper's own 6x results (joint 3.23 vs quant-only 1.00) show the staged policy is not optimal. 'These results validate the Gini stability finding' -- PPL ratios at 32K do not measure Gini stability; the correct claim is 'are consistent with'. 'attention sparsity profiles calibrated at short context transfer to 32K tokens without recalibration' -- inferred from two models on one dataset, and Gini is never re-measured at 32K. (b) VAGUE REFERENT. 'This weak correlation means the two signals provide complementary information' -- 'this' points at rho = 0.194 over 22 layers, which is not significantly different from zero, and weak correlation does not entail complementarity. 'The reduction generalizes' -- from n = 2 models. 'The cost-model's marginal-gain ranking is robust enough that the inverted default does not collapse on the late-bottleneck models' -- 'does not collapse' has no threshold; the number it points to is 1.56 at 6x, a 56% PPL increase. (c) THING-VS-PROCESS CONFLATION. 'Profiling' denotes both the pipeline artifact and the per-input activity ('The full profiling pipeline adds 61--109%' vs 'fixed profiles ... reduce the per-input overhead'). 'Allocation' denotes both the solver run and its output plan ('the allocation differs at every CR'; 'per allocation' as a latency unit). 'Importance' denotes both the parametric weight w_l and the measured LOO sensitivity, which have opposite signs on Llama-2-13B. (d) FALSE PRECISION. NIAH values quoted to one decimal (93.3%, 86.7%, 73.3%, 26.7%) from cells of 15 items -- 93.3% is 14/15, so the sole LayerBudget-vs-KIVI retrieval advantage in the paper is one question. 'reduces output KL divergence by 96%' from a single 0.249 -> 0.009 pair on one model at one CR. '118--119%' quoted to three figures against an unnamed reference. 'MAE 3.1%' from one model. 'We audited 1,779 PPL checkpoints' -- a precise count offered in place of the per-method effective-CR table that would actually settle the question.

Thesis reconstructed without headings: 'Because per-layer sensitivity to eviction and to quantization differ, a greedy per-layer joint allocation of token count and bit-width -- quantizing before evicting, protecting early layers, and mean-filling what is evicted -- gives near-lossless KV compression at 2-4x across 7B-72B models.' Topic-sentence audit, listing only paragraphs that fail. (1) The Related Work MoE-nD paragraph: its topic sentence is 'The closest concurrent work is MoE-nD', but its evidence is a head-to-head result table, a loss concession, a second method (LayerBudget-KV) introduced for the first time in Related Work, and a baseline-provenance caveat. Four distinct claims under one topic sentence, none of them positioning -- this is a Results/Limitations paragraph misfiled, and the LayerBudget-KV introduction belongs in Method. (2) The Byte-CR Reconciliation appendix: no identifiable thesis-mapping topic sentence; it is an erratum against the paper's own table, and it concedes the table should not be cross-referenced with the rest of the paper. Candidate for deletion-and-recompute, not revision. (3) The paragraph beginning 'On LongBench (16 English tasks, Table~[REF]' has no predicate and no topic sentence -- it terminates mid-clause and the Limitations enumeration begins. A paragraph whose topic sentence cannot be identified is itself the finding, and here the entire Analysis-section conclusion is missing. (4) Key-findings bullets 1, 2 and 4 in Main Results are three restatements of one claim ('LayerBudget ranks first among token-reducing methods'); bullets 3 and 5 are two restatements of 'KIVI is fine on PPL but bad on NIAH'. Five bullets carry two claims. (5) The paragraph in Section 3.5 arguing 'quantize first emerges naturally' maps to the thesis but its evidence does not map to it: the evidence offered is the ablation observation that at low CR no tokens are evicted at all, which shows the budget was loose, not that the marginal-gain ordering produced the behavior.

I have only the LaTeX source; ppl_scaling.pdf, allocation_heatmap.pdf and signal_curves.pdf were not provided, so their rendering, labels and internal consistency are UNVERIFIABLE and I flag that as a gap in what I can certify. What is checkable from captions and text is already defective. (i) Both mechanism figures are on TinyLlama-1.1B, a model that appears in no results table anywhere in the paper -- the entire visual argument for the method's premise is on a model that is never evaluated. (ii) The signal_curves caption asserts 'Weak correlation (rho=0.194) confirms complementary signals'; over 22 layers rho = 0.194 has p ~ 0.39, so the caption states as confirmed a quantity indistinguishable from zero, and 'weak correlation' does not imply 'complementary' in any case. (iii) The ppl_scaling caption claims 'LayerBudget (bold) outperforms all eviction methods and matches KIVI at 2--3x' -- 'matches' is the honest word and it concedes the paper's central comparison; but the same figure cannot show the 4-6x region without showing KIVI winning, so the caption's framing needs to be checked against what the panel actually plots. (iv) The allocation_heatmap caption promises 'Bar height = token fraction; color = precision' at 2x-6x on TinyLlama, which if plotted would show all bars at full height for 2x-3.5x (the paper states no tokens are evicted there) -- i.e. the figure most likely visualizes the regime in which the method does nothing, and this should be stated. Recommend regenerating both mechanism figures on a model that appears in the results.

(a) ANONYMITY: no author names, institution, funding, or acknowledgment text; external links absent; self-citations are not identifying. However there is an aggressive priority posture toward concurrent work -- 'The closest concurrent work is MoE-nD, which independently arrives at the same ... joint formulation' plus a novelty claim ('To our knowledge, no prior online, training-free method jointly optimizes per-layer (n_l, b_l)') that the 2026 record contradicts (RDKV, HqeKV, ARKV, ThinKV). Not a de-anonymization, but a priority claim I would ask the AC to discount. Two forward-looking commitments -- 'we will update against their official code at camera-ready' and 'For the camera-ready we will regenerate Table X' -- presume acceptance and read as carried-over rebuttal text; they should be removed, and the corresponding numbers fixed before submission rather than promised after. (b) COMPLETENESS: '\input{checklist}' is present at the end of the document, so the checklist is nominally included, but its contents are not in the provided source and I cannot verify that the required items -- in particular the NeurIPS LLM-usage declaration -- are present and answered. UNVERIFIABLE, flagged. (c) FORMAT: the neurips_2026 style file is used with no margin or font manipulation that I can see, and no \vspace abuse beyond routine -0.05in/-0.2in around figures. Page count is unverifiable without the PDF, but the truncated Analysis section is consistent with content having been cut under page pressure. The source as given would NOT compile: '\begin{table[t]' is malformed (missing brace, stray bracket), and '\section{Analysis' and '\textbf{Downstream accuracy.' both leave braces unclosed. A submission whose source does not build is a real desk-reject risk under 'you must format your submission using the LaTeX style file for that year', and at minimum the compiled PDF cannot correspond to this source.

Three theory-to-implementation mismatches, one of them fatal. (1) w_l. THEORY NAMES: 'Importance weights each layer's contribution to eviction sensitivity' (Section 3.2). IMPLEMENTATION COMPUTES: w_l = sigma(5 x (1 - l/(L-1) - 0.3)), a fixed monotone decreasing function of layer index with two hand-set constants and no dependence on any measurement of the model. These are not the same object: one is a per-model sensitivity estimate, the other is a positional prior. The paper then measures the real sensitivity by LOO on three architectures, finds the sign reverses on Llama-2-13B and vanishes on Qwen2.5-14B, and still runs every end-to-end number under the prior. What is proved/argued (allocate by sensitivity) is not what is run (allocate by depth). FATAL per gate (b), and no experiment in the paper runs the recommended per-architecture variant end to end. (2) Q. THEORY NAMES: 'a quality model' whose maximization under a byte constraint is cast as MCKP. IMPLEMENTATION COMPUTES: sum_l (n_l/S)^{1-g_l} x F(b_l) x w_l -- an additive combination of a per-layer product of an attention-mass fraction, a cosine similarity and a sigmoid. No claim is established that this sum is monotone in, or even correlated with, the PPL ratio that every table reports; only the coverage factor is validated (one model, MAE 3.1%, and against attention mass, not quality). The additive-across-layers form also contradicts the paper's own LOO evidence that single early layers dominate. So the optimizer optimizes an object whose relation to the evaluated metric is unestablished, and the greedy's '118--119%' figure certifies performance against an unnamed reference on that unvalidated surrogate. (3) 'Quantize first, evict last'. CLAIMED SEMANTICS: an emergent property of the marginal-gain ordering ('The quantize first behavior emerges naturally from the marginal gains: at low CR, Delta Q/Delta M for a bit-upgrade exceeds that of a token-add at almost every layer'). WHAT THE EVIDENCE SHOWS: the ablation states that at 1.5-3.5x 'no tokens are evicted' at all, i.e. the budget is loose enough that the allocator restores every token regardless of ordering, and 'Gini has no effect'. The claimed emergent hierarchy is, in the regime where it is claimed, an artifact of a non-binding constraint -- and the algorithm additionally hard-initializes b_l = 4 for all layers, so the fully-quantized state is an initialization, not a discovered solution. (4) A fourth, smaller mismatch: the allocator's token granularity is Delta n = 8 while the vLLM deployment rounds to 16-token blocks, so the deployed allocation is not the allocation the solver returns; the vLLM result is reported only at S=512 where this matters most.

Contributions in the order claimed, each with its isolating experiment and measured marginal effect. C1 (billed FIRST): per-layer (n_l,b_l) formalization + quantize-first greedy with calibrated fidelity constants. Isolating experiments: component analysis A1 and the budget sweep (combined vs importance-only). Measured effect: at 1.5-3.5x, exactly zero by the paper's own words ('All signal variants are equivalent ... no tokens are evicted, and Gini has no effect'); at 4x, 1.04 vs 1.06 (2pp) while quant-only is 1.00; at 6x, joint 3.23 vs quant-only 1.00 (Mistral) and 45.09 vs 1.01 (Llama-2-7B) -- i.e. NEGATIVE against the trivial alternative of quantizing everything, at every cell in A1. The precision-level sub-ablation A3 is degenerate: {4,16} and {4,8,16} agree in all four cells to within 0.01, so the three-level bit set contributes nothing measurable either. C1 is therefore a contribution billed as primary whose isolating experiment shows zero or negative marginal effect -- a fatal credit-assignment defect. C2: inverted importance. Isolating experiment: the importance-direction ablation. Measured effect: real and large at 6x (Mistral 1.283 vs 3.231 sigmoid; Llama-2-7B 2.52 vs 45.09), modest at 4x (1.008 vs 1.039; 1.002 vs 1.166), and confined to the CR regime where the method already loses to KIVI. Its generality is refuted by the authors' own LOO on Llama-2-13B. C3: mean-fill. Isolating experiment: the Analysis section KL and PPL comparisons plus median/random-fill controls. Measured effect: the largest in the paper (KL 0.249->0.009; PPL 45.09->1.13) -- but computed against the sigmoid configuration, not the declared inverted default (see P5). C4: the 17-baseline controlled comparison -- evidence, not a contribution, and compromised by chance-level baselines (P4). C5: 16K-32K validation -- real, but two to three models, one dataset, PPL only. C6: 72B scaling -- real, but LB 1.06 vs KIVI 1.00 at 6x and RULER 98 vs 99 at 2x. RANKING BY MEASURED EFFECT: C3 >> C2 >> C5/C6 > C1 (<= 0). RANKING IMPLIED BY THE ABSTRACT: C1 first. The orderings are inverted. The honest fix is to demote the joint allocator and rebuild the paper around mean-fill and importance direction -- both of which are, notably, orthogonal to and composable with plain KIVI.

(a) ONE SENTENCE IN THIS COMMUNITY'S VOCABULARY: 'A training-free, online, per-layer joint allocation of KV-cache token budget and quantization bit-width, solved greedily by marginal quality-gain per byte under a global memory constraint, plus mean imputation of evicted KV entries.' The sentence forms cleanly, so there is no vocabulary failure -- the paper is written for the right community. (b) TERMS A PC MEMBER WOULD HAVE TO LOOK UP OR WOULD DISPUTE: 'coverage law' (an asserted power law, not a law); 'fidelity constants' (cosine similarities repurposed as multiplicative quality factors); 'inverted importance' (a positional prior, not an importance measure); 'MoE-nD framing' used as a baseline name; 'mean-fill' (fine, but idiosyncratic vs the literature's 'imputation'). None is disqualifying. (c) MISPLACED MECHANISM: none -- everything here (Gini profiling, greedy MCKP allocation, INT4/INT8 KV, PagedAttention block rounding) is squarely efficient-inference/ML-systems. (d) THE REAL FIT PROBLEM IS THE BAR, NOT THE ROOM. Related work positions against 2024-2025 methods plus one 2026 concurrent paper, while the venue's own 2026 accepted literature is absent: STAR-KV (ICML 2026 Spotlight, 20x with custom kernels and 3.1x throughput), KVTC (ICLR 2026, 20-40x), Layer-DefensiveKV (ICLR 2026, RULER 91.4 at 20% cache), TurboQuant (ICLR 2026, 3-bit K / 2-bit V with Triton kernels and vLLM integration). Against that bar, a 2-6x envelope with sub-1x decode speedup and +2.6-12.2% TPOT overhead is not a NeurIPS/ICLR main-track result. The evaluation also ignores the methodology results this community now enforces (query-aware vs query-agnostic ordering; the sdpa-vs-eager backend effect of -0.221 on RULER, larger than most method gaps; matched-budget auditing) and the de-facto KVPress harness. I would not forward this to a different community -- I would forward it to a systems workshop or a second-tier venue after the memory accounting, the harness, and the KIVI comparison are rebuilt. Mis-venuing per se is not the defect; being a generation behind the venue's own frontier is.

(a) EXPECTED METRICS FOR THIS PROBLEM, 2026. REPORTED: WikiText-2 PPL ratio; MMLU; GSM8K (200 samples); NIAH at 4096; LongBench-v1 (16 English tasks); RULER at 4096 (one model only); decode TPOT; KV memory savings; prefill profiling overhead. OMITTED: LongBench-v2 (v1 is now considered dated -- and the v1 numbers here are broken, see P4); InfiniteBench; SCBench (the KV-cache-centric benchmark, with cache reuse and multi-turn shared context); HELMET; RULER across 4K-128K and its 13 subtasks (only a single 4K point on Qwen2.5-72B); effective bits per token, now the common currency alongside CR; end-to-end throughput and peak memory at long context; batch-size scaling; reasoning-regime benchmarks (AIME, MATH-500, GPQA-Diamond, LiveCodeBench) that dominate the current long-output sub-field; confidence intervals on anything except a single unquantified paired-bootstrap mention. (b) DO OMITTED METRICS THREATEN HEADLINE CLAIMS? Yes, two of them fatally. Effective bits/token under a single byte denominator would directly test 'ranks first ... at memory-matched comparison', and the one memory table in the paper already indicates it would reverse it (LB 12,939 KB @1.07 vs KIVI 9,990 KB @1.01). RULER/LongBench-v2 at >= 16K would test 'matches Full KV', and the paper's only >= 16K evidence is WikiText-2 PPL -- a metric that is nearly insensitive to retrieval failure, which is precisely the failure mode the paper claims to fix relative to KIVI. (c) UNMEASURED TERMS IN THE PAPER'S OWN OBJECTIVE: the objective is sum_l C x F x w, and NONE of the three factors is validated against end quality on the models where results are reported -- C is validated on one model against attention mass (not quality), F is a cosine similarity never linked to PPL or task accuracy, and w is never validated at all (and is measured to have the wrong sign on Llama-2-13B). The optimized quantity Q itself is never plotted against the reported PPL ratio. An unmeasured objective is a defect independent of field convention. (d) WORKLOAD REGIME MISMATCH: the claims are stated over the long-context regime ('KV cache compression is most impactful at long context'), but the headline model-suite table, all ablations, the head-to-head tables, MMLU, GSM8K and the memory/latency tables run at S = 512-1024, where the KV cache is 67-287 MB -- not a bottleneck on either the 3090 or the A100. Only two models have any 32K evidence, on one dataset, one metric.
